newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU slot rules deal could include sales, conditions.
newsitem.headline: EU slot rules deal could include sales, conditions.

text.p: The European Commission may impose conditions on airlines' rights to airport slots on busy routes in return for allowing them to sell unwanted slots, a Commission official told Reuters on Friday.
The plan, one of several being considered in a Commission review of EU slot allocation rules, would add conditions to airlines' existing "grandfather rights" to airport landing and take-off slots.
"We are looking at a number of options," said the official, adding that another idea under review would allow slot sales in return for time limits on airlines' "grandfather rights".

"If you limit grandfather rights, you certainly then have to ask how are those slots going to be distributed," said the official, adding that such an option was unlikely to fly because of strong opposition from EU national governments.

Plans by European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock to legalise a suspected "grey market" in illegally traded slots at the EU's busier airports went awry last year after objections by his competition counterpart, Karel Van Miert.
The competition commissioner said the idea would unfairly increase dominant carriers' edge over smaller airlines.

"My feeling is that some sort of solution which is economic in nature is going to come out, it might also be combined with some specific operational conditions which say that the size of the market would also govern the size of the aircraft. That's going to reduce the number of slots you need.

"Until now, we have seen airlines competing on frequency with some of them using smaller aircraft in order to have more frequency which uses up slots like mad. It would be very useful if we could change that mechanism," the official added.

The official said the system might involve a rolling review of all airport slots, for example 10 percent per year over 10 years, when slot holders on busy routes would have to agree to fly larger aircraft or give up slots.

EU slot allocation rules are of prime importance to scrutiny of the planned British Airway/American Airlines alliance by EU and British competition authorities, in which the two are likely to have to surrender slots at London's busy Heathrow airport in return for the deal's approval.
The airlines want to sell the slots, a practice outlawed by existing slot allocation rules and insisted upon by a senior Commission official speaking to Reuters on Friday.

Allowing BA/American to benefit from a future rule change on slots would be "legally impossible", said the senior official, who added: "The two issues are separate animals and cannot impact on each other."
